page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, with the running head "DEDICATIO." centred above it. No margin notes, no page number and no catchword.

main_text.p: ftes, victoriis suis efferati, impotentius deinceps populum Dei infestare occiperent. Quamobrem ille florem juventutis in Martis palaestra strenue exercendum, ut, prout res ferret, ad patriam, religionemque tutandam excubarent, prudenter censuit. Cujus exemplum pii & cordati omnes, qui religionem & pietatem, qua nihil sanctius & antiquius mundus habet, contra Sathanae insidias & insultus creberrimos sartam tectamque cupiunt, & pro muneris sibi impositi ratione praestare tenentur, religiose & studiose sibi imitandum statuunt. Cum enim Sathanas, Regni sui promachus acerrimus, & Regni Christi hostis infensissimus, ferale illud Regnum suum multiplici & furore, & mendaciorum mole & substructione stabilire indefesso, flagrantissimoque studio satagat, atque satellites suos juratos eandem in rem, alios quidem potentia, diritatis affectu, & leonina ferocia, alios vero serpentina calliditate, & ἀπατητικῷ[?] λόγῳ discepatrice, & deceptrice facultate armet, non tantum pii omnes adversus furoris & crudelitatis ictus, spiritu roboris a Deo ipso uncti, constantiae invictae scutum obtendunt: sed etiam Ecclesiarum & Scholarum doctores Divinitus χειροπο-

page.notes: The running head is set in capitals above the text and is given as the running title. Greek words in the text are italic; the first Greek word (ἀπατητικῷ λόγῳ) is doubtful in its letters and is marked [?]. The last word of the page breaks off at the line end ("χειροπο-") and continues on the next page. Some letters in the scan are faint, notably the ends of lines.
